answer: Each epoch, every identity must solve a fresh sequential puzzle bound to its own public key inside a live window: it cannot be parallelized, precomputed, or split across clones, so running a thousand fakes needs a thousand sequential solves, not one. A walnut of that rule is that wall-clock time, not money, is the scarce input. Peers re-run a sample of solutions, and a copied answer is caught because the echo of one computation on two keys never matches. The pearl is the audit trail: each solve chains to the last, so a farm keeps paying compute every epoch while honest agents pay once.
